## Keywords

{{< glossary proposition truth-value boolean-variable negation conjunction disjunction exclusive-or implication operator-precedence >}}

## 16.1 Propositions

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- A proposition is a statement that is either true or false.
- In game code, a proposition is a bool such as hasKey.
- Orders, questions and opinions are not propositions.
- **Do it:** Write three propositions about a racing game. Which one is true now?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/propositions.png)
:::
::::

## Try it 1 · Propositions

a) Is "The player has the key." a proposition?
b) Is "Open the door!" a proposition?
c) Is "3 > 5" a proposition, and what is its value?

::: {.answer}
a) Yes, it is true or false.
b) No, it is an order.
c) Yes, and it is false.
:::

## 16.2 NOT, AND and OR

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- NOT p is true when p is false, and in C# it is !p.
- p AND q is true only when both are true: p && q.
- p OR q is true when at least one is true: p || q.
- **Do it:** Try the four cases in Logic Lab. When is p AND q true?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/not-and-or.png)
:::
::::

## Example · Two doors

The player has the key (p = T) but no torch (q = F).
**Which doors open, and does the trap fire?**

::: {.reveal}
1. The iron door needs p ∧ q: T ∧ F = **F**, so it stays shut.
2. The wooden door needs p ∨ q: T ∨ F = **T**, so it opens.
3. The trap fires on ¬q: ¬F = **T**, so it fires.
:::

## Try it 2 · NOT, AND, OR

a) p = T and q = F. What is p ∧ q?
b) p = T and q = F. What is p ∨ q?
c) p = F and q = F. What is p ∨ q?

::: {.answer}
a) false
b) true
c) false
:::

## 16.3 XOR: exactly one

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- p XOR q is true when exactly one of the two is true.
- When both are true or both are false, XOR is false.
- In C#, XOR of two bools is p ^ q.
- **Do it:** Is "a sword or a bow, one at a time" OR or XOR? Why?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/xor-implies.png)
:::
::::

## Try it 3 · XOR

a) p = T and q = T. What is p XOR q?
b) p = F and q = T. What is p XOR q?
c) Which operator does the rule "the alarm rings when a door or a window opens" need?

::: {.answer}
a) false
b) true
c) OR
:::

## 16.4 IF–THEN

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- p → q is false only when p is true and q is false.
- It has the same value as ¬p ∨ q.
- When p is false, the rule says nothing, so p → q is true.
- **Do it:** Which case breaks "if the level is finished, all coins are collected"?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/xor-implies.png)
:::
::::

## Example · Checking the crown rule

The rule says: "If the player has the crown, then the boss is defeated."
**Which case is a bug, and how does the code find it?**

::: {.reveal}
1. Crown and boss defeated: T → T = T, so the rule is kept.
2. Crown and boss alive: T → F = **F**, so this is the bug.
3. The code checks **hasCrown && !bossDead** and reports the bug.
:::

## Try it 4 · IF–THEN

a) When is p → q false?
b) p = F and q = F. What is p → q?
c) Which expression has the same value as p → q?

::: {.answer}
a) when p is true and q is false
b) true
c) ¬p ∨ q
:::

## 16.5 Brackets and order

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- The order is NOT first, then AND, then OR.
- Brackets are always computed first.
- So p ∧ q ∨ r means (p ∧ q) ∨ r.
- **Do it:** p = T, q = F, r = T. What is (p ∨ q) ∧ r?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/precedence.png)
:::
::::

## Example · The last gate

The boss is alive (F), the player has no key (F), but a torch (T).
**Does the gate open with and without brackets?**

::: {.reveal}
1. With brackets: F ∧ (F ∨ T) = F ∧ T = **F**, so the gate stays shut.
2. Without brackets: (F ∧ F) ∨ T = F ∨ T = **T**, so the gate opens.
3. The second one is a bug, so the rule needs the brackets.
:::

## Try it 5 · Brackets

The facts are p = T, q = F and r = T.

a) What is p ∨ q ∧ r?
b) What is ¬p ∨ ¬q?
c) Which operator is computed first, AND or OR?

::: {.answer}
a) true
b) true
c) AND
:::

## 16.6 Logic in game code

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Every if and while in a game checks a condition.
- && and || stop early when the result is already known.
- So enemy != null && enemy.isAlive never crashes without an enemy.
- **Do it:** Write the condition "jump when on the ground and not stunned".
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/logic-code.png)
:::
::::

## Try it 6 · Code

a) Which condition means "jump when on the ground and not stunned"?
b) Which condition means "warn when the health is below 20 or the time below 10"?
c) Why must enemy != null come first in the condition?

::: {.answer}
a) onGround && !stunned
b) health < 20 || time < 10
c) && stops early, so isAlive is never read without an enemy.
:::

{{< sim file="sims/door-logic.html" poster="sims/door-logic.png" title="Door Logic: the condition for each door" kind="game" task="**The story:** in the dungeon of Torch Hall, every door, trap and lever has a rule in words. **Play:** choose the condition that the game code must check." >}}

## Try it 7 · The last gate (harder)

a) Which condition opens the gate for a defeated boss and the key or a torch?
b) Which condition checks that the crown rule is kept?
c) Which operator does the lever with "exactly one switch up" need?

::: {.answer}
a) bossDead && (hasKey || hasTorch)
b) !hasCrown || bossDead
c) XOR, written left ^ right
:::

## Summary

- A proposition is true or false, and in code it is a bool.
- AND needs both, OR at least one, and XOR exactly one.
- p → q is false only when p is true and q is false.
- NOT comes first, then AND, then OR, and brackets change the order.
- In code, && and || stop early, so the safety check goes first.
